audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page connects Acceleration Gate to Thundering Blow, so the reader is told to fear both at once with no way to tell which one is available.
audit.why: They are the same slot. Riot lists E as 'Thundering Blow / Acceleration Gate' on one 20/18/16/14/12/10 cooldown. If Jayce drops a gate to accelerate a Shock Blast, his hammer knockback is gone for up to 20 seconds at rank 1 — that is the moment a 650-range Justice Punch and a 275-range taunt actually reach him. This is the decisive interaction in the matchup and it was absent from both layers.
audit.corrected: Written into the trading rules, cooldown block, Key Ability Interactions, winCon, level-3 phase, the don't and the loading tip: a gated poke means no knockback, so walk in.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page states flatly that Jayce's damage is physical and that 'your shield is physical-damage reduction only, so it won't blank his poke' — twice in the content layer and again in whys[1].
audit.why: Half true and worded wrong. Shield of Durand reduces all damage and is amplified against magic; it is not 'physical reduction'. And Thundering Blow deals MAGIC damage, while Mercury Hammer's first attack after a swap 'deals additional magic damage'. So the amplified half of your W is exactly what answers his hammer combo — which is the trade you are told to take anyway.
audit.corrected: Reworded so the poke is physical (build armour) but the hammer step-up is magic and the amplified reduction bites it — which is why you hold W for the step-up rather than the poke.

audit.whatIsWrong: His stance swap is treated as a free, instant choice, and the full layer says 'Reassess his ultimate too'.
audit.why: Mercury Cannon / Mercury Hammer is his R, a flat 6-second cooldown — he cannot change stance more often than that, so catching him in the wrong form is a real window. Mercury Cannon's first attack also reduces the target's Armor AND Magic Resist, which is why his burst lands harder than his listed damage suggests.
audit.corrected: 6s stance timer named at the level-6 phase and in the foe-wants line; the Mercury Cannon resistance shred added to the late spike and whys[6].

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Track Shock Blast' appears eight times with no cooldown attached.
audit.why: Jayce's Q is 16/14/12/10/8/6 — 16 seconds at rank 1, which is enormous for a poke tool, and his E is 20 seconds. Early on he genuinely cannot re-poke, and nothing on the page told the reader that.
audit.corrected: 16s Q and 20s E written into the cooldown block, do's, trading rules, tldr, winCon and the loading tip.

audit.whatIsWrong: The don't reads 'E-punch into his Shock Blast (it catches you mid-dash)'.
audit.why: Shock Blast is a skillshot orb; nothing in Riot's text makes it interrupt a dash. The mistake that actually loses this lane is stepping into taunt range while he still holds hammer Thundering Blow, because the knockback removes you from the 275-range release.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the Thundering Blow rule in both the don'ts list and Common Mistakes.

edits.before: Jayce owns the first two levels — Shock Blast fired through his Acceleration Gate hits like a poke laser and you have only Winds of War to answer with, no W up yet. Don't walk up to last-hit into a gated Shock Blast; soak with the tornado's center column and accept the chip. Remember his damage is physical, so Shield of Durand is just flat damage reduction here, not the magic sponge it is elsewhere — its value is the taunt on release. The instant you have all three abilities at Level 3, hold W for when he swaps to hammer stance and steps in to Thundering-Blow you; release the taunt, then E Justice Punch through him for the knockup. His burst is real, but baiting his hammer commit into a charged W-taunt is how he dies.
edits.after: Jayce owns the first two levels — Shock Blast fired through his Acceleration Gate gains missile speed, range and damage, and you have only Winds of War to answer with. Don't walk up to last-hit into a gated Shock Blast; soak with the tornado's centre column and accept the chip. His poke is physical, so armour is the buy, but note that Thundering Blow deals magic damage — the amplified half of Shield of Durand answers his hammer combo, not his cannon poke. That is why you hold W for the step-up. The instant you have all three abilities at level 3, watch which button he spends: Acceleration Gate and Thundering Blow share one slot on a 20s cooldown, so a gated poke means he has no knockback and your taunt reaches.

edits.before: This is the even stretch where your kit is online but his poke keeps pace. Your trade only works on his terms: bait the Shock Blast, then punish the hammer step-up — release Shield of Durand to taunt him, E-knockup, and burst back while he's locked, because you can't win a ranged poke exchange against a lethality marksman. At 6 your edge finally appears: Hero's Entrance. Even if Jayce is zoning you out of lane, shove the wave and drop your global onto a fight elsewhere — the landing knockup and taunt make you the best map button on the Rift, and that's how you beat a laner you can't 1v1.
edits.after: This is the even stretch where your kit is online but his poke keeps pace. Your trade only works on his terms, and the tell is his E: Acceleration Gate and Thundering Blow are the same button on a 20s cooldown at rank 1, so the second he gates a Shock Blast he cannot knock you out of the taunt. Walk in on that, release Shield of Durand, punch the knockup, and burst while he is locked. At 6 your edge appears: Hero's Entrance. Even if Jayce is zoning you out of lane, shove and drop your global on a fight elsewhere — that is how you beat a laner you can't 1v1.

edits.before: Jayce reclaims the late lane. He builds lethality and keeps you at Shock Blast range, gapping you with the Acceleration Gate and Thundering-Blow knockback before you ever taunt — and your shield is physical reduction here, so it barely dents a poke pattern that never overcommits. Your damage and tankiness plateau while his combo keeps scaling. Stop trying to win the side lane: your value is Hero's Entrance map presence and being the teamfight engage. Group, flag your R onto his carry-line or a caught teammate, and let the taunt-knockup do what your 1v1 cannot.

Second correction: the page said 'your shield is physical-damage reduction only'.
